run_by: Dinis Cruz, who pasted the review to newsroom.writer
summary: The warning about Rovo in automation is supported, but the article blurs whose permissions an agent uses: the agent's creator does not pass on their access; the executing identity is the requester in chat, the connection account in automation, or the agent's own account. It also misclassifies audit logs as a boundary, overgeneralises connector setup and the size of the gap, and overstates the Ruflo and Northstar evidence.

facts.notes: Checked against Atlassian's identity, sharing, automation, connector and governance documentation, ROVO-837, PromptArmor, riskmandate.ai, the merged Ruflo page and the Northstar disclosure. The reviewer's quotation of an Atlassian support article on automation connections could not be found on Atlassian's pages when the newsroom checked; ROVO-837 carries the equivalent wording. The sentence 'This issue does NOT occur in Rovo Chat' in ROVO-837 is the reporter's, not Atlassian's.

claims.notes: Prevalence claims without population evidence; audit logs presented as preventive; Ruflo and Northstar evidence overstated.

findings.quote: Some paths run as somebody else. When a Rovo agent runs from Jira Automation, it uses the permissions of the automation's connection user, typically whoever created the rule
findings.issue: Effective permissions depend on the agent's configured identity and how it is invoked: in chat with User's account, the requester's; in automation, the connection account's, which need not be the rule's creator or the agent's creator; with Agent's account, the agent's own. 'Typically whoever created the rule' implies more than Atlassian documents.
findings.evidence: Atlassian: configure a Rovo agent's identity; knowledge sources for agents; ROVO-837; best practices to automate agents safely
findings.suggestion: Explain the three cases and name the connection account as the deciding identity.

findings.quote: links to pages the triggering user cannot view
findings.issue: ROVO-837 documents disclosure of a restricted page reference in an automation's output; opening the link still failed. It does not show access to the page or its full content. The reporter notes it does not occur in Rovo Chat.
findings.suggestion: Say what was disclosed: a reference, not the page; and that the risk is reading with one identity and publishing to a wider audience.

findings.issue: Atlassian now documents agents with their own accounts; its 6 October announcement still lists wider agent-account controls and a non-human identity inventory as coming. Availability should be checked per tenant. Agent's-account agents also make content shared with them available to their users.
findings.evidence: configure a Rovo agent's identity; Team '26 Europe announcement, 6 October 2026; best practices to automate agents safely
findings.suggestion: Describe agent accounts as documented, with controls to check in the tenant, and add the sharing consideration.

findings.quote: was safe while nobody knew the link
findings.issue: The file was less discoverable, not safe; Drive sharing settings still apply.
findings.evidence: Atlassian: connect Google Drive to Rovo

findings.quote: Connectors are set up by an administrator with broad rights, and then each user links their own account
findings.issue: True of Google Drive, not of every connector: synced, direct and Smart Link connectors differ in setup, indexing and authentication.
findings.evidence: Atlassian: Rovo connector types; Rovo connectors admin guide
findings.suggestion: Say it depends on the connector.

findings.quote: administrators can narrow it to selected groups
findings.issue: Restricting who creates agents (by group) and who uses a particular agent (individuals only) are different controls.
findings.evidence: Atlassian: Rovo agent permissions and governance

findings.quote: classification, redaction of sensitive data and audit logs, sit in the boundary row too
findings.issue: Audit logs record events; they do not prevent them. Classification identifies sensitivity and bounds only through a policy acting on it. Only blocking and redaction can prevent data moving.
findings.evidence: Atlassian's governance blog separates data protection, autonomy controls and record-keeping
findings.suggestion: Classify each mechanism by what it does.

findings.quote: The administrator's allowlists for which drives and sites are indexed
findings.issue: Indexing allowlists control indexing, not everything Rovo can fetch at run time with the user's access; MCP server permissions govern that server's operations, not every Rovo path, on Atlassian's documentation.
findings.evidence: Atlassian: connect Google Drive to Rovo; Rovo connector types; configure Atlassian MCP server permissions

findings.quote: I found no statement from Atlassian on a fix
findings.issue: The PromptArmor report is accurate as a historical report; present exploitability is unverified.
findings.suggestion: Separate the reported attack from its current status.

findings.quote: for most organisations that is most of the company
findings.issue: No population evidence for the size of the gap or how often controls are only prompt instructions.
findings.suggestion: Say the gap can be substantial and must be measured per deployment.

findings.issue: The library is example policies; connectors to customer systems are built per engagement and none is a product yet.

findings.quote: from £10 for the pack to £1,500 reviewed
findings.issue: The pricing page marks the £500 and £1,500 levels specified, never run, as of 15 September 2026.

findings.quote: enforced it in Ruflo's evaluator, in real time, on every memory operation
findings.issue: The merged page documents an external adapter governed by a pinned copy of the evaluator; it does not alter Ruflo's running policy or restrict other shell or MCP tools.
findings.suggestion: Narrow to operations through the adapter.

findings.quote: overpays $458 in a day; the design with three policies gets all thirteen right
findings.issue: The Northstar results come from a scripted simulation with synthetic cases and no model.
findings.suggestion: Say thirteen synthetic cases in a scripted simulation.

findings.quote: Under the UK Corporate Governance Code, boards already have to determine the principal risks
findings.issue: The Code applies to specified listed companies, not every UK board.
findings.evidence: UK Corporate Governance Code, Principle O
findings.suggestion: Add: for companies the Code applies to.
